beginner.stem: Which history line belongs to Sulfur?
options: Sulfur, called brimstone, was known from volcanic deposits and from metal ores long before it was classed as an element.
Carl Wilhelm Scheele prepared oxygen around 1772, and Joseph Priestley published the same gas in 1774 after heating mercuric oxide.
Jöns Jacob Berzelius found a red residue in the slime of a sulfuric-acid plant at Falun in 1817.

beginner.stem: How does the catalog describe the discovery of Sulfur?

Humphry Davy had isolated potassium from molten potash with a voltaic pile.
